messages:
marta_cust: Hey team, seeing ~5% of requests return 401 from our private deployment behind an F5 LB. Works fine if we bypass the LB and call the backend directly. Can someone help?

alice_support: Sorry you're hitting this — can you share a short repro curl and a packet capture showing the header behaviour? 

marta_cust: repro curl: 
```
curl -v -H 'Authorization: Bearer eyJ...' https://api.mycompany.internal/v1/predict
```
From tcpdump on the LB -> backend interface I see incoming request contains Authorization header, but backend app logs show no Authorization.

alice_support: hm intermittent -> could be an iRule or header whitelist on the F5. Do you have the iRule config? Also which virtual server profile (HTTP vs TCP) is in front?

marta_cust: it's an HTTP virtual server. here's the small iRule snippet (sanitized):
```
when HTTP_REQUEST {
  if { [HTTP::header exists "X-Cust-Auth"] } {
    HTTP::header remove Authorization
    HTTP::header insert "X-Cust-Auth" "[HTTP::header Authorization]"
  }
}
```

raj_enginfra: oh this is the key — the iRule is removing Authorization and moving it to X-Cust-Auth. Our backend is expecting Authorization header for token introspection. If the header gets removed some backends (or pooled connections) won't see X-Cust-Auth.

alice_support: do you know why the iRule was added? was it for cookie/token rewriting or to stop forward of opaque cookies to upstream?

marta_cust: ops added it ages ago to centralize auth for legacy services. New services (like our Redwood node) weren't updated to trust X-Cust-Auth. We thought the header was forwarded but looks like it's being removed entirely in some cases.

toni_se: security note — preserving raw Authorization across the LB can be sensitive. If you choose to preserve it, please confirm audit logging and key rotation. Otherwise make sure all upstreams are updated to read the new header consistently.

alice_support: feasible options: (1) update iRule to preserve Authorization and also set X-Cust-Auth (dup) so both old and new apps work, or (2) update upstream to use X-Cust-Auth consistently, or (3) have iRule always copy rather than remove. Quickest rollback: copy instead of remove.

raj_enginfra: proposed minimal change:
```
when HTTP_REQUEST {
  if { [HTTP::header exists "X-Cust-Auth"] } {
    # copy instead of remove to avoid racing with pooled connections
    HTTP::header insert -m after Authorization "X-Cust-Auth" "[HTTP::header Authorization]"
  }
}
```
This duplicates header; should preserve behavior and avoid missing Authorization on some backend connections. We'll test with a canary pool.

marta_cust: can you test with my pod? I can hit a debug endpoint that dumps headers.

alice_support: sure. raj, can you push to staging then to prod canary? I'll run the debug curl in staging.

deploy-bot: config-change raj_enginfra pushed iRule update to staging at 2026-02-12T14:32:10Z. CI: passed.

alice_support: staging verified — debug endpoint shows both Authorization and X-Cust-Auth present. Replaying load for 30m, previously reproducible 401s dropped to 0.

marta_cust: running canary in prod now — initial telemetry looks good, auth 401 rate back to baseline. Thanks! :tada:

toni_se: please open a short change request documenting why Authorization is preserved and the retention/audit plan. We'll review for security posture.

marta_cust: opened CHG-4512 with details and link to this thread.

alice_support: closing here — if the 401s recur, please re-open and we'll escalate to eng-sre. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: deployment to prod canary completed at 2026-02-12T15:04:55Z.

marta_cust: confirmed resolved for now, thanks everyone.
